what_this_is: The Page Indexing (Pages) report as it stood on 2026-09-21, transcribed from reports/gsc-baseline-2026-09-21.md, which recorded it from the Search Console UI by hand.
why_it_is_kept_separate_from_the_cohort: It covers a DIFFERENT URL SET: the 91 core, destination, region and guide pages that were live then. The 500 Atlas pages this analysis is about were published afterwards and are not in these counts. It is historical context for how Google treats this property, not index state for the cohort, and nothing may read it as the cohort's status.
source: manual reading of the Search Console interface, not an API call and not an export
redirect_and_duplicate_urls: www.livdar.com/ (www redirects to the apex, expected)

performance_at_the_time.note: both windows give the same totals because every impression fell on 18 and 19 September 2026

the_technical_state_at_the_time: all 91 URLs returned 200, were index,follow, canonical to themselves and present in the sitemap, and 30 were indexed. The baseline's own conclusion was that the first bottleneck is indexing rather than titles or CTR.
what_that_reason_means: Google knows the URL exists and has chosen not to spend crawl budget on it yet. It is a discovery and priority signal about the property, not a verdict on the page's content, and it is the reason 58 of the 64 not-indexed URLs carried.
the_follow_up_this_file_is_owed: the baseline asked to be re-read on or after 2026-10-05 and compared. That re-read has not happened and is what scripts/atlas/gsc-url-inspection.mjs and scripts/atlas/analysis/import-gsc-pages-report.py exist to supply.
